name: Improper Control of Generation of Code ('Code Injection')
principle: The product builds code from externally influenced input and executes or loads it without strict neutralization. Attacker-controlled syntax can change control flow and execute unauthorized code.
detection_signals: Java GroovyShell.evaluate(...), Janino ExpressionEvaluator.cook(...), or JavaCompiler.getTask(...) compiles externally built strings
C/C++ luaL_dostring(...), luaL_loadstring(...), PyRun_SimpleString(...), Tcl_Eval(...) receives tainted char* or std::string
JavaScript eval(...), new Function(...), setTimeout(string), or setInterval(string) receives user-controlled data
Python eval(...), exec(...), compile(...), or __import__(...) receives user-controlled data
PHP eval(...), assert(string), include/require path or file content is user-controlled
Dynamic function/method/class name is concatenated from input then invoked via reflection, call_user_func, getattr, or Class.forName
negative_signals: User input selects a key in a fixed Map/switch/enum dispatch table; no code string is generated
Interpreter/compiler sink argument is a constant literal or trusted bundled resource only
External plugin/JAR/script is loaded only after signature or SHA-256 digest verification against a pinned value
Allowlist validates the entire token and maps it to a fixed permitted function name before invocation
Parser handles data with typed conversion such as Integer.parseInt/int()/JSON parser instead of eval/exec
false_defense_traps: Alphanumeric-only validation before dynamic invocation still allows dangerous names such as system, exec, exit, or Class.forName
Denylisting dangerous substrings is bypassable with aliases, encoding, reflection, imports, or concatenation
Sandbox/jail alone limits OS impact but does not prevent application-level compromise or jail escape issues
ast.literal_eval avoids code execution but can still cause memory or stack exhaustion on untrusted deeply nested input
Client-side validation does not protect server-side code generation sinks
verification_focus: Can any externally influenced value reach a code-evaluating, code-compiling, code-loading, or dynamic invocation sink as syntax rather than data?

consequence_chains.consequence: Unauthorized code execution with confidentiality, integrity, and availability loss

consequence_chains.trigger: Attacker input is inserted into dynamically evaluated code
consequence_chains.consequence: Eval injection and arbitrary control-flow modification

consequence_chains.trigger: Attacker-controlled code is written to a file/resource and later included or loaded
consequence_chains.consequence: Persistent code execution on later use

consequence_chains.trigger: Untrusted template expression is rendered by a template engine

patch_principle: Refactor to avoid dynamic code generation; use fixed dispatch tables or typed parsers
Use strict allowlists of complete permitted tokens and map them to constant functions or templates
Never concatenate untrusted data into code, script, template, include path, or compiler input
Verify integrity and origin before loading external code artifacts or plugins
If dynamic execution is unavoidable, run it in a constrained sandbox as defense in depth
